stories.title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
stories.simple_summary: India is requiring apps that block spam calls to share their spam data with telephone companies. One company is upset because they want to keep this information private since it's valuable to their business.
stories.why_it_matters: Mostly a business and regulatory issue — this doesn't change anything for ordinary phone users right now.

stories.title: Tilly Norwood’s press tour is going about as well as you’d expect for an AI
stories.simple_summary: A company created an AI person named Tilly Norwood to do interviews and promote things, but the AI is malfunctioning — it even started speaking Chinese in the middle of a conversation.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI still isn't reliable enough to represent companies in public — nothing you need to worry about for your own business.

stories.title: A startup that builds other startups raised $100M and is all-in on physical AI
stories.simple_summary: A company called Vantora helps big industrial companies create new AI businesses by doing the startup work for them. They just raised $100 million to expand this idea.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly relevant to large corporations — small business owners won't be directly affected.

stories.title: Anthropic is operating a lab that conducts biology experiments
stories.simple_summary: An AI company called Anthropic is running a biology lab to test whether AI can help discover new medicines. Meanwhile, some of the same people warn that powerful AI could be dangerous.
stories.why_it_matters: This is early research that might help with medicine in the distant future, but nothing affecting you today.

stories.title: AI hallucination nearly triggers US military operation
stories.simple_summary: An AI system gave incorrect information that almost caused the US military to start an operation. The incident shows that AI can confidently give you wrong answers, and people need to understand this limitation.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a reminder that you shouldn't trust AI completely without checking its answers — especially for important decisions.

stories.title: Anthropic’s first embedded evaluator is … Accenture?
stories.simple_summary: A consulting company called Accenture has been hired by Anthropic to check whether their AI is working safely and reliably. This is a very risky job.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech professionals — nothing affecting ordinary people directly.

stories.title: OpenAI and Microsoft knew they were starting a ‘doom loop’ for the web
stories.simple_summary: Secret court documents show that OpenAI and Microsoft knew their system was scraping the internet for training data in ways that could damage websites, but they did it anyway.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows the companies ignored their own warnings about harm for business reasons — it affects internet creators and the health of the web, though not your personal daily life.

stories.title: World model companies are keeping a lot of secrets
stories.simple_summary: Companies building a new type of AI called 'world models' are keeping quiet about what they're actually making, even though they've raised lots of money.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly interesting to investors and tech watchers — nothing you need to know about right now.

stories.title: A new kind of AI model from a ChatGPT inventor is thrilling developers
stories.simple_summary: A person who helped invent ChatGPT created a new type of AI model that helps programmers write software faster and cheaper than before.
stories.why_it_matters: Over time, this could make software development less expensive, but it's too early to know if this affects your business.

stories.title: Virginia governor creates an AI task force and moves to restrain data centers
stories.simple_summary: Virginia's governor is creating a task force to manage AI and is putting limits on huge data centers (the buildings that power AI) to give local communities more say in whether they get built.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live in Virginia, this could affect what your community looks like and your electricity costs, but otherwise this is local policy.

stories.title: Disney’s first CTO led an AI startup it once accused of copying its characters
stories.simple_summary: Disney just hired the former leader of a startup called Character.AI to be their chief technology officer — even though Disney sued this same startup for supposedly copying Disney characters.
stories.why_it_matters: This is interesting corporate news but doesn't affect you unless you work in entertainment.

stories.title: Google’s new ‘CC’ is an AI agent that helps families run their households
stories.simple_summary: Google created an AI assistant that helps families organize their household by managing calendars, making shopping lists, planning meals, and filling out forms.
stories.why_it_matters: If your family uses Google services, this could become a helpful tool for organizing your home — like having a personal assistant for scheduling and planning.
